title: Fifteen companion documents describe shell scripts that no linter can check
foundBy: session agent, reviewing the cs-* companion documents on 2026-09-02
details:
`cs-lint surface` checks a documented interface against the binary the repository builds. It asks one tool, named by `toolPath` in `.cs-lint.yaml`, and that tool is `bin/cs-sandbox`.

Fifteen companion documents under `image/rootfs/home/.local/bin` describe shell scripts instead. They cover `cs-claude-remote`, `cs-codex-remote` and `cs-opencode-remote`, each with its `_STATUS`, `_OUTPUT`, `_SESSIONS` and `_FORGET` companion. The scripts sit beside them in that same directory. No linter reads either side, so nothing compares the two.

The drift this allows has already happened. The OpenCode sandbox profile documented `cs-opencode-remote-status <name>` without the `-t` flag, while the script had parsed `-t` since it was written. A manual read on 2026-09-02 found it. Nothing else would have.

A Go test in `internal/cli` can close the gap. Each script parses its flags in a `case` block a test can read. The test can compare that set against the flags the matching document names, in both directions. It can also assert that every `cs-*` tool in the directory has a document, and every document a tool.

Naming `CS_SANDBOX.md` in `docs.extraDocs` on 2026-09-02 brought that one document under `surface`. The fifteen cannot follow, because `surface` needs a binary to ask and these describe scripts.
